name: comparator-kickback
description: Charge kicked back into the comparator's input nodes by one decision, over PVT: the peak disturbance at the 1 kohm source impedance README.md's kickback row is stated at, and the residual differential/common-mode displacement of a floating high-impedance input -- including its signal-dependent part, the only component that cannot be absorbed as an offset.
claim: PLACEHOLDER DUT. sim/dut.json binds sim/dut/placeholder_comparator.spice (id placeholder-v1, provenance placeholder). This record substantiates the harness -- that the kickback measurement path (peak disturbance at a realistic source impedance, plus near-zero-referenced residual probing) genuinely runs over the full PVT grid -- and is NOT evidence toward README.md#target-specification's Kickback row until design/comparator.sch exists and sim/dut.json is repointed at it (spec/porting-plan.md next step 1). The disturbance couples through the placeholder decision stage's explicit c_fb stand-in (sim/dut/placeholder_comparator.spice), not a real input pair's C_gd.

kick_1k_peak_mv.description: THE ROW-FACING NUMBER AND THIS BENCH'S CORNER-SENSITIVITY ANCHOR: peak disturbance of an input node, relative to its own driving source, during one decision, with a 1 kohm series source impedance and 100 fF of node capacitance -- the exact condition README.md's kickback row states. The bounds here are a sanity envelope only; the SPEC bound is deliberately not encoded while README.md's target-specification table stays DRAFT and a placeholder is bound. The per-axis floors make --sabotage-corners fail: the peak is set by the input devices' C_gd/C_gs and by the front end's bandwidth, both of which move with process and temperature. Floors calibrated from this experiment's first committed 45-point record (named in this experiment's README.md, run --no-write during issue #8 development), with margin below the observed weakest slices (process 3.53%, temperature 0.71%, supply 14.55%). Temperature is genuinely the weak axis here (this placeholder's kickback path is a fixed 5 fF C_fb stand-in, not a real transistor C_gd, so its temperature coefficient is small) -- its floor is set accordingly, still comfortably above the ~0% a runner stuck on one temperature would produce.

kick_sigdep_nv.description: THE COMPONENT THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS: the difference between the residual differential kickback at a 100 mV residue and at a 1 mV residue, on a floating high-impedance input. A residue-INDEPENDENT disturbance is indistinguishable from comparator offset; only the residue-DEPENDENT part is an irreducible error.

kick_resid_small_nv.description: Residual differential displacement left on a floating 1 pF input node after one decision, at a 1 mV residue -- the part of the kickback that never recovers because there is no low-impedance path to restore it.

kick_cm_nv.description: Common-mode displacement of the two floating input nodes over one decision. Rejected by a differential comparator to first order, but a large common-mode kick would move the operating point the offset and noise records were taken about.

kick_resid_raw_uv.description: THE SAME RESIDUAL, MEASURED THE NAIVE WAY, in the record to make a methodology point rather than a design one: ngspice's ~6-significant-digit `meas` result precision quantizes a ~1 V node difference at ~1 uV. kick_resid_small_nv measures the identical physical quantity through a near-zero-referenced probe and resolves it ~1000x finer.

q_resid_small_ac.description: The residual differential kick expressed as CHARGE on the 1 pF floating node, in attocoulombs, so a reader whose input capacitance differs from this bench's can rescale it.

dout_1k_end.description: The 1 kohm-driven instance must still DECIDE CORRECTLY while its own kickback is disturbing its input.

dout_float_small_end.description: the same for the floating instance at a 1 mV residue -- the harder case, because nothing restores the injected charge.

dout_float_big_end.description: the same at a 100 mV residue.

notes: TWO SOURCE IMPEDANCES, BOTH IN THE RECORD, AND NEITHER IS AN IDEAL VOLTAGE SOURCE. An ideal source restores the injected charge instantly and reports ~0 kickback however bad it is. Instance A uses the 1 kohm impedance README.md's kickback row is stated at (peak disturbance); instances B and C use a 1 pF node through 1 Gohm, RC = 1 ms against a ~30 ns cycle (residual charge).
ONLY THE SIGNAL-DEPENDENT PART IS IRREDUCIBLE. A residue-independent kick is indistinguishable from comparator offset; that is why B and C sit at 1 mV and 100 mV residues.

THE RESOLUTION FLOOR IS A PROPERTY OF THE MEASUREMENT AND IT IS IN THE TABLE. ngspice's `meas` returns ~6 significant digits, so differencing two ~1 V node levels quantizes the answer at ~1 uV. kick_resid_raw_uv shows the floor; kick_resid_small_nv resolves the same physical quantity ~1000x finer via a near-zero-referenced probe.
MISMATCH IS OFF (the plain mos corner set). Kickback and offset are separable and are budgeted separately.
THE INPUT NODE IS A LUMPED CAPACITANCE, not a modelled driving network. There is no CDAC, no sampling switch and no sequencer here.

PLACEHOLDER CAVEAT. The coupling from the placeholder's decision stage back to the front end is an explicit 5 fF/side stand-in for a real latch input pair's C_gd (declared in sim/dut/placeholder_comparator.spice), not an extracted capacitance.
